ledger.title: 📋 Ledger — Transaction Register
ledger.filter.description_placeholder: search the description or an amount...
ledger.filter.one_by_one: To look at one by one
ledger.filter.one_by_one_help: The movements of the places where you buy everything that you have not looked at yet: they have the generic category.
ledger.metric.totals_help: Internal transfers and card settlements are left out of the totals: they move money between your own accounts, they are neither income nor expenses.
ledger.metric.excluded: {n} internal transfers or card settlements in the table are left out of the totals ({out} out, {inc} in).
ledger.sort.label: Sort by
ledger.col.description_help: You can rewrite it in your own words (for example 'Home mortgage' instead of 'Rapporto'): only this movement changes, the bank's text stays as it was.
ledger.description_empty: Row {row}: the description cannot be empty, the previous one was kept.
ledger.own_name.ask: You named this movement "{name}". There are {n} more movements like it: same bank text (without numbers and dates) and same amount.
ledger.own_name.ask_variable: You named this movement "{name}". There are {n} movements with the same bank text but different amounts (from {low} to {high}): it looks like an installment that changes.
ledger.own_name.ask_future: You named this movement "{name}". Should the next movements like it (same bank text, same amount) get this name too?
ledger.own_name.all: Rename all ({n}), also in future imports
ledger.own_name.same_amount: Only those with the same amount ({n})
ledger.always.ask: You put **{n}** movements of **{name}** in **{cat}**. Always like this?
ledger.always.done: From now on {name} goes to {cat}, in the next imports too.
ledger.own_name.category_rule: Also fix the category {cat} for "{name}" (a rule: it holds for future imports too)
ledger.own_name.done: "{name}": {n} movements, and the next ones like them.
ledger.col.rule_select_help: Tick a movement to write a rule from it: the "Create rule from selection" box appears below the table. A rule holds for every equal movement, also in future imports. With several movements ticked you can instead mark them checked together, with the button below the table.
ledger.col.date_help: Date of the operation, as the bank writes it.
ledger.col.raw_help: The movement's text as the bank writes it. It is never changed.
ledger.col.income_help: Money that came into the account.
ledger.col.account_help: The account or card the movement comes from.
ledger.col.type_help: What the movement is: spending, income, card spending, or a transfer between your own accounts, out or in.
ledger.col.cat_sub_help: How you spent, or where the money came from. Changing it here holds for this movement only: for every movement of the same counterpart use the Counterparts step or a rule (📏 column).
ledger.col.context_help: A label of yours across categories, for example Holiday or Work.
ledger.col.source_help: Who decided the category: the model (🧠), a rule of yours (📏), you by hand (👤), the history of movements (📚), or a place where you buy everything (🛒).
ledger.col.flag_review_help: ⚠️ = to review: the product is not sure of the category.
ledger.col.flag_transfer_help: 🔄 = transfer: money moved between your own accounts, neither spending nor income.
ledger.col.transfer_help: Tick it when the movement moves money between your own accounts: it becomes a transfer, does not count as spending or income, and loses its category.
ledger.one_rule_at_a_time: ⚠️ One rule can be created and applied at a time — select a single row
ledger.rule_exists_update: ⚠️ Rule already exists — it will be updated. It will match {n} transactions
ledger.select_row_for_rule: Select a row (📏) to create a rule
ledger.edit_hint: ✏️ Edit **{cat}**, **{ctx}** and **🔄 {transfer}** directly in the table, then click **{save}**.
ledger.col.validated_help: Tick it once you have verified the movement is real: the money really went out or came in. It is not about the category, and it does not carry over to the movements of future imports.
ledger.no_transactions: No transactions found with the selected filters.
ledger.subcategory_mismatch: ⚠️ Row {row}: subcategory «{sub}» does not belong to «{cat}». Valid subcategories: {valid}
ledger.wrong_direction: Row {row}: "{cat}" belongs to the other direction (spending on money in, or the other way round), not saved.
ledger.fan_out.found: Found **{n}** similar transactions not categorised yet. Apply the same category?
upload.model_downloading: ⏳ The AI model is still downloading (see the banner above). Import becomes available as soon as it is ready — usually 3-15 minutes on first launch.

review.rerun_llm_empty: 🔄 Reprocess with LLM (no transactions pending review)

review.bulk_save_rule: Save as rule (reusable in the future)

rules.title: 📏 Categorization Rules
rules.caption: Rules are applied before the LLM. By editing or deleting a rule you can also update transactions already categorized by that rule.
rules.no_rules: No rules saved. Create your first rules below or from the Review page.
rules.run_all_caption: Apply all active rules to **all** transactions in the ledger. For each transaction the first matching rule (by priority) wins. Unmatched transactions remain unchanged.
rules.run_all_confirm: I confirm: I want to overwrite categories of all transactions matching a rule
rules.run_all_done: ✅ Done — **{matched}** transactions updated ({cleared} marked as reviewed).
rules.context_help: If set, it will be assigned to the transaction. Leave '— nessuno —' to not change it.
rules.also_update_txs: Also update the {n} transactions already categorized by this rule
rules.grid_saved: Rules updated: {n}. The movements they cover follow them.
rules.own_names_caption: The name you gave a bank movement, for every one with the same text (without numbers and dates) and the same amount. Removing it does not change the names already given: it counts for future imports.
rules.giroconto_check: It is an internal transfer (money between your accounts)
rules.giroconto_help: Matching transactions become internal transfers instead of getting a category.
rules.preview_no_match: No existing transactions match this pattern.
rules.new_rule_also_apply: Also apply to the {n} transactions already in the ledger
taxonomy.title: 🗂️ Taxonomy — Categories and Subcategories
taxonomy.caption: Changes are saved immediately to the database. New categories/subcategories are instantly available in Review and Rules.
taxonomy.color_help: This category's colour in every chart of the app. Its subcategories take a shade of it. Changing it is an expert choice.
taxonomy.color_fallback: Fallback category: always grey in charts, like "other".
checklist.title: ✅ Checklist: transactions by month and account
checklist.caption: One row per month (current at the top), one column per account. The value is the transaction count; **—** means no transactions for that month.
checklist.no_data: No accounts and no transactions found. Add accounts from **Settings** and import movement files.
checklist.filter_accounts_help: Leave empty to show all accounts.
checklist.hide_empty_help: Hides months where no account has transactions.
checklist.no_filtered_data: No data to show with the selected filters.
settings.title: ⚙️ Settings
settings.country_caption: Country where your bank accounts are located. Improves automatic recognition of international brands (e.g. Migros CH vs Migros TR, Lidl IT vs Lidl DE).
settings.desc_language_caption: The language in which bank statement descriptions are written. Used by the LLM categorizer to interpret transactions correctly.
settings.ui_language_caption: The language used for menus, labels and filters in the app. / La lingua per menu, etichette e filtri dell'app.
settings.giroconto_mode_caption: Defines how internal transfers (between your own accounts) appear in the ledger and analytics. *Show* includes them as neutral rows; *Exclude* hides them.
settings.owners_caption: Names of account holders (comma-separated). Automatically removed from descriptions before sending to remote LLMs to protect privacy.
settings.use_owners_giroconto: Use owner names to identify internal transfers
settings.use_owners_giroconto_help: When enabled, transactions whose description contains an owner name are automatically marked as internal transfers.
settings.contexts_caption: Define the contexts to classify transactions (e.g. Everyday, Work, Vacation). You can assign a context to each transaction from the Ledger.
settings.force_schema_help: When enabled, files are imported automatically even when schema classification has low confidence. Useful for expert users who prefer speed over manual review. A warning is shown if confidence is < 0.50.
settings.force_schema_active: ⚠️ Schema review is disabled — all files are imported with the detected schema.
settings.test_mode: Test mode (first 20 rows per file only)
settings.test_mode_help: Imports only the first 20 rows of each file to quickly verify schema classification.
settings.test_mode_active: ⚠️ Test mode active — only the first 20 rows will be processed.
settings.max_tx_amount_help: Columns with median value above this threshold are discarded as amount columns (e.g. 'Reference' columns with numeric IDs). Increase only if you have real transactions above €1,000,000.
settings.accounts_caption: Define your bank accounts. The account name is used as a stable key for transaction dedup (independent of the imported file name). Associate each file with the correct account on the Import page.
settings.no_accounts: No accounts configured. Add one to associate it with imported files.
settings.schema_cache_caption: Spendif.ai stores the structure of imported files to speed up subsequent imports. If a file was imported with the wrong schema (e.g. missing columns), clear the cache and re-import.
settings.clear_schemas_help: Removes all schemas from cache. On the next import, files will be re-analyzed.
settings.backend.openai_compatible: OpenAI-compatible (Groq, Together AI, Google AI Studio…)
settings.llama_cpp.caption: Local backend based on llama.cpp — no external server required. Download a GGUF model and Spendif.ai uses it directly.
settings.llama_cpp.model_path_help: Leave empty to automatically use the first .gguf file found in ~/.spendifai/models/
settings.llama_cpp.gpu_layers_help: -1 automatic GPU offload, 0 use CPU only
settings.llama_cpp.select_local_placehol: Select to auto-fill path and context window…
settings.llama_cpp.no_models: No GGUF model found in ~/.spendifai/models/. Download one below.
settings.llama_cpp.n_ctx_help: Number of tokens in the context window. Higher values require more RAM. The model's native limit is shown after Test LLM.
settings.ollama.pull_help: Download or update the model on Ollama
settings.ollama.connection_error: ❌ Cannot connect to Ollama at {url}. Verify the server is running.
settings.test_llm_help: Verify that the LLM backend responds correctly
settings.test_llm_validation_error: ❌ LLM responded but with validation error: {error}
settings.test_llm_connection_error:
❌ Cannot connect to the backend. Verify URL and that the server is running.

`{error}`
settings.test_llm_auth_error:
❌ Authentication error. Verify the API key.

`{error}`
settings.compat.caption: Compatible with any API exposing `/v1/chat/completions` (Groq, Together AI, Google AI Studio, etc.)
settings.cat_backend_toggle: Use a different model for categorization
settings.cat_backend_toggle_help: When enabled, document classification and transaction categorization use separate LLM models.
settings.cat_backend_caption: The model below is used only to assign category and subcategory to transactions. Document classification (column recognition, account type) continues to use the main model configured above.
settings.cat_backend_same: ℹ️ Categorization uses the same model as classification.
settings.power_user_caption: Preset for expert users: enable all advanced options, disable confirmations, maximize automation.
settings.power_user_applied: Power User profile applied! • Forced import without schema confirmation • Max amount: 10M€ • Press 💾 Save to confirm.
settings.nsi_map_caption: Links recognised brands to your categories. It is created on first launch and rebuilt by itself whenever you change the taxonomy — but that rebuild takes a few minutes and lands in the middle of your next import. You can get it out of the way here.
settings.nsi_map_status_ok: ✅ {n} tags mapped, aligned with the current taxonomy.
settings.nsi_map_status_stale: ⚠️ The map is not aligned with the current taxonomy ({n} tags). It will be rebuilt on the next import, or now.
settings.nsi_map_status_empty: The map has not been built yet. Without it, recognised brands still go through the AI.
settings.nsi_map_rebuilding: Mapping brands onto your taxonomy… this takes a few minutes.
settings.nsi_map_failed: ⚠️ Rebuild failed — an active AI backend is required. The static fallback map stays in use.
settings.reset_taxonomy_warning: ⚠️ This operation **replaces** all categories and subcategories with the default template for the selected language. Already categorized transactions are **not** modified.
settings.reset_taxonomy_confirm: I confirm: I want to overwrite the current taxonomy
onboarding.title: 👋 Welcome to Spendif.ai
onboarding.subtitle: Initial setup — it will take less than 2 minutes.
onboarding.no_taxonomy: No default taxonomy found in the database.
onboarding.step0.title: 🌍 Language and Format
onboarding.step0.caption: Choose the taxonomy language and date/amount formats. We detected your browser language — you can change it.
onboarding.step0.country_caption: Used to better recognise international brands (e.g. Lidl, McDonald's, Migros) in your transactions.
onboarding.step1.title: 👤 Owner Names
onboarding.step1.caption: Enter the name(s) of the account holder(s), separated by comma. They are used to automatically detect **internal transfers** between your own accounts and to clean transaction descriptions.
onboarding.step1.hint: 💡 Example: `John Doe, Jane Doe` — include all name variants as they appear in bank statement files.
onboarding.step1.label: Owner name(s)
onboarding.step1.warning: ⚠️ Enter at least one name to continue.
onboarding.step2.title: 🏦 Bank Accounts
onboarding.step2.caption: Add your bank accounts, cards and investment accounts. The **account name** is a free label (e.g. *BankX checking*, *Visa Card*). You can add more accounts anytime from ⚙️ Settings.
onboarding.step2.no_accounts_warning: ⚠️ No account added. You can continue but transaction dedup may not be stable.
onboarding.step3.title: ✅ Summary
onboarding.step3.caption: Review settings and click **Start** to apply them.
onboarding.step3.llm_recommended: HW: {gpu} · {ram} GB RAM → Recommended: **{name}** ({size} MB). Will be downloaded on first import.
onboarding.step3.llm_none: No compatible model found. Configure manually in Settings.
onboarding.step3.start_disabled_tooltip: We're still downloading Spendif.ai's brain. The button will enable as soon as it's ready.
onboarding.step_taxonomy.title: 🗂️ Default taxonomy
onboarding.step_taxonomy.caption: These are the categories that will be created for you. You can customise them any time from Settings → Taxonomy.
onboarding.step_taxonomy.customize_later: Uncheck ✓ to exclude a category or subcategory, or edit its name inline. Expand the panel to see subcategories. Further edits remain available from Settings → Taxonomy.
onboarding.step3.taxonomy_counts: **{cat_kept}** of {cat_total} categories · **{sub_kept}** of {sub_total} subcategories will be created.
onboarding.step3.taxonomy_edits: Edits: {cat_disabled} categories excluded · {cat_renamed} renamed · {sub_disabled} subcategories excluded · {sub_renamed} renamed.
onboarding.step3.waiting_model: Waiting for AI model download to finish
onboarding.step3.model_error: AI model download failed: {error}. Go to Settings to retry.
onboarding.preparing_categories.title: Setting up your categories…
onboarding.preparing_categories.caption: One-time operation (~5 min): the AI model is mapping places to your chosen categories. Everything will be ready for your first import.
bulk_edit.title: ✏️ Edit several movements
bulk_edit.caption: Select a transaction and apply category, context or internal transfer status to all similar transactions. You can also save a deterministic rule.
bulk_edit.with_giroconti_help: Internal transfers have no category: show them only to remove the transfer mark.
bulk_edit.recent_hint: Counterparts of the last {n} movements, the ones with more movements first. For an older one, search it by description.
bulk_edit.same_desc_info: **{same_desc}** tx with same description · **{same_raw}** with same original description · **{similar}** similar (Jaccard ≥ 35%)
bulk_edit.section2_caption: Re-run counterpart extraction and/or categorization on a selection of transactions. The LLM backend configured in Settings will be used.
bulk_edit.extract_counterpart_help: Re-extracts the merchant/counterpart name from the original description
bulk_edit.recategorize_help: Re-applies deterministic rules and LLM for category/subcategory
bulk_edit.no_tx_found_criteria: No transactions found for the selected criteria.
bulk_edit.apply_same_desc_giro: Also apply to {n} tx with same description
bulk_edit.apply_same_desc_ctx: Apply to {n} tx with same description
bulk_edit.save_as_rule_help: Creates a 'contains' rule that applies this category to all transactions with similar description in the future.
bulk_edit.apply_same_desc_cat: Apply now to {n} tx with same description
bulk_edit.giro_no_category: Transaction marked as internal transfer — category correction is not applicable.
bulk_edit.section4_caption: Define selection criteria, check how many transactions will be deleted and confirm. **This operation is irreversible.**
bulk_edit.filter.desc_placeholder: filter by text in description or original description...
bulk_edit.no_filter_warning: ⚠️ No filter set — set at least one criterion before proceeding.
bulk_edit.no_match_filter: No transactions match the selected filters.
bulk_edit.confirm_delete_instruction: To confirm, type exactly **`DELETE`** in the field below and press the button.
bulk_edit.confirm_delete_placeholder: type DELETE to enable the button
bulk_edit.section5_caption: Transactions with same **date**, **original description** and **amount** present on different accounts. Typically caused by overlapping imports (e.g. account statement + card statement).
bulk_edit.dup_groups_found: Found **{n_groups} groups** of duplicates — **{n_extra} excess transactions** (one per group is the original).
bulk_edit.dup_delete_info: The button deletes **excess copies** keeping the first transaction per group (by import date order).
bulk_edit.confirm_dup_placeholder: type DELETE to enable the button

guided.checklist.no_accounts: Tell me which accounts you have: just the name, files come later.

nav.llm_models.desc: Per-phase LLM backends, account credentials and operations
llm_models.title: 🤖 LLM Models
llm_models.caption: Configure a dedicated model for each pipeline phase (classifier, cleaner, categorizer, footer). Leave empty to use the main backend's model.
llm_models.status.title: Current status
llm_models.phase.classifier.caption: Detects document type, maps columns, decides debit/credit convention. 1 LLM call per file.
llm_models.phase.cleaner.caption: Extracts the merchant/payer name from the bank description. Batched, dozens of calls per file.
llm_models.phase.categorizer.caption: Assigns category + subcategory to each transaction. Batched, frequent.
llm_models.phase.footer.caption: Identifies header/footer rows that aren't transactions. Rarely invoked.
llm_models.phases.title: Per-phase configuration
llm_models.phases.caption: Each phase can use a different model. Enable the override only where you want to specialise.
llm_models.phase.use_main: Use the same model as the main backend
llm_models.phase.use_main_help: When on, this phase inherits the model of the main backend (Settings).
llm_models.phase.using_main: This phase uses the main backend.
llm_models.phase.local_llama_cpp.n_ctx_h: 0 = auto-detect from the GGUF, capped at 16384.

update.version_line: Version {latest} is out. You are running {current}.
update.cmd.homebrew:
Update from Terminal:
```
brew update && brew upgrade --cask spendifai
```
update.cmd.dmg: Download the new DMG from [Releases](https://github.com/spendifai/spendif-ai/releases/latest) and drag it to Applications again.
update.cmd.deb: Download the new .deb from [Releases](https://github.com/spendifai/spendif-ai/releases/latest) and install it with `sudo apt install ./spendifai_*.deb`.
update.cmd.rpm: Download the new .rpm from [Releases](https://github.com/spendifai/spendif-ai/releases/latest) and install it with `sudo dnf install ./spendifai-*.rpm`.
update.cmd.arch: Download the new .pkg.tar.zst from [Releases](https://github.com/spendifai/spendif-ai/releases/latest) and install it with `sudo pacman -Syu && sudo pacman -U ./spendifai-*.pkg.tar.zst`.
update.cmd.msix: Download the new MSIX from [Releases](https://github.com/spendifai/spendif-ai/releases/latest) and double-click to install it.
update.cmd.winget:
Update from PowerShell:
```
winget upgrade SpendifAi
```
update.restart_hint: Then quit and reopen the app.
settings.update_check_help: At startup the app asks GitHub for the latest published version and compares it with the one you are running. The check runs in the background: the app never waits on the network.
settings.update_check_privacy: What leaves your computer: only the question "what is the latest version". No budget data, no transactions, no identifier. GitHub sees your IP address, as any website you open does. Turn this off and the app contacts nobody, but you will not know when a new version ships.
settings.update_history_caption: Local history, it never leaves this computer. Useful when reporting a problem: it says exactly which build you came from.
update.cmd.git_source:
Update from the install directory:
```
git pull && uv sync
```
upload.emulated_arm: This build is x64 running under emulation on a Windows ARM machine, where the local AI model cannot run at all: the emulator does not implement the CPU instructions it needs, and a test of the model fails with Windows error 0xc000001d. Choose a hosted model in Settings, or use a native x64 machine. Everything else in the app works normally.

counterparts.col_categorized_help: Tick it if this counterpart always has the category shown. Once is enough: it becomes a rule for the movements already imported and for those of future imports. It says how you spent, it does not confirm the movements are yours: that is done in the Ledger, one by one.
counterparts.uncheck_ignored: {name} keeps the category set by you: to change it, pick another one in the row.
counterparts.confirm_no_category: {name}: choose a category before ticking it.
counterparts.guided.criterion:
**Once per counterpart is enough.** Tick **Always like this** when a counterpart always has the category shown: from then on its movements, including those of future imports, get that category on their own and we will not ask again. Counterparts that already have one of your rules do not show up.

The criterion: give a category to 8 spending movements out of 10 from {date_from} to {date_to}. Counterparts are listed with the most movements first: they are the ones that repeat, often written in different ways, and one tick covers them all.

Here you decide how you spent, not whether you spent: to confirm a movement is real, tick it in the Ledger.
counterparts.guided.progress: You have given a category to {checked} spending movements out of {total}. To reach 8 out of 10, {missing} are missing: the first {needed} counterparts in the list are enough.
counterparts.guided.progress_one: You have given a category to {checked} spending movements out of {total}. To reach 8 out of 10, {missing} are missing: the first counterpart in the list is enough.
counterparts.guided.reached: You have given a category to {checked} spending movements out of {total}: more than 8 out of 10. You can move on, or keep ticking if you like.
counterparts.guided.optional: The goal is a suggestion: you can move on whenever you want, even before reaching it.
counterparts.guided.all_categorized: Every spending counterpart of the period has a category set by you. You can move on.
counterparts.guided.no_spending: There is no spending to categorize in this period. You can move on.
counterparts.guided.saved: Thanks to the counterparts you have already ticked, {n} movements for {amount} of spending were categorized on their own: you do not need to look at them.
counterparts.guided.small_singles: The {n} counterparts with a single movement up to {limit} ({amount} in all) are not asked: in a typical year of the last {years}, the ones up to this amount make less than {cap}% of your spending. Deciding them would mean looking at them one by one; they keep the proposed category and do not count toward the goal.
counterparts.guided.show_small: Also show the counterparts with a single movement up to {limit}: {n} of them, {share}% of the spending imported
mixed.title: 🔀 Mixed categories
mixed.none: No counterpart with movements in more than one category to look at. You can move on.
mixed.intro: These counterparts have movements in more than one category. **If it is a mistake**, choose the right category and press *It is always this*: it applies to every movement, including those of future imports. **If it depends on what you bought** (the supermarket where you also buy electronics), no rule can tell them apart, since the name is always the same: look at them one by one. The ones you have already given a category are not asked again: next time you will see only the new ones.
mixed.optional: This step is optional: you can move on whenever you want.
mixed.multi_todo: A place where you buy everything: {n} movements to look at one by one.
mixed.multi_btn: Always like this: I buy everything here

mixed.only_new: You have already sorted out {done}: only the {todo} that came with the last import are left.

income.title: 💶 Income
income.guided.criterion:
**Once per counterpart is enough.** Here is the income from {date_from} to {date_to}, largest first, without the money moved between your own accounts. Check the category and tick **Always like this**: from then on that counterpart's income, also in the imports to come, gets that category on its own.

Income comes from few counterparts and each one weighs: there is no goal here, look at all of them.
income.guided.refunds: A refund or a return on a purchase is not income: pick the spending category (for example Groceries), so it lowers that spending.
income.guided.one_by_one: {names}: they have spending too, so the choice applies only to their income already loaded and does not become a rule.
income.guided.all_checked: All the income of the period has a category set by you. You can move on.
income.guided.none: There is no income to categorize in this period. You can move on.
transfers.title: 🔁 Transfers
transfers.none: No transfers to look at: the money moved between your accounts has both sides. You can move on.
transfers.intro: When you move money from one of your accounts to another, the statement it leaves shows money out and the one it reaches shows money in. They are neither spending nor income: here you check that the two halves were put together.
transfers.optional: This step is optional: you can move on whenever you like.
transfers.older: {n} more transfers to look at are older than 4 months: we do not ask about them.
transfers.pairs_help: Same amount, out of one account and into another, but not sure enough to decide alone. Answer Yes if it is a transfer, No if it is not: a pair you turn down is not proposed again.
transfers.singles_help:
This money went to, or came from, an account you have not loaded. Tell us where: the answer holds for every movement with the same counterpart, in the imports to come too.

- **My account, not loaded yet**: add it in Settings and load it from the Check List, the pair closes by itself.
- **My account, not followed** (a deposit, a savings account): it stays a transfer, out of spending.
- **Another person**: it is not a transfer, it becomes spending (or income).
transfers.reason.both: same amount, {days}, both read as a transfer
transfers.reason.one: same amount, {days}; one of the two was {kind}
transfers.reason.none: same amount, {days}, neither read as a transfer
transfers.settled: {n} more transfers are already settled (sure or already approved): we do not propose them again.
guided.checklist.held: **{n} movements set aside**: the date read is in the future, so they did not enter the ledger and count nowhere. Usually the date was misread. Fix the date and import them, or discard them.
guided.checklist.held_help: When swapping day and month gives a past date, the correct date is already proposed: check it before importing.

guided.checklist.held_still_future: {description}: the correct date is still in the future, the movement stays set aside.
guided.checklist.held_duplicate: {n} movements were already in the ledger: they were not inserted twice.

intermediaries.caption: PayPal, SumUp and the like only pass the money on to the merchant, like a debit card. In movements written "PAYPAL *TRENORD SRL" the counterpart is TRENORD SRL. The list starts from the product's own, grows by itself when a prefix appears before several different merchants in your movements, and here you can add or switch off entries.
intermediaries.active_help: Switched off, the descriptions of future imports keep the prefix. It stays off after updates too.
intermediaries.deactivate_note: Switching an intermediary off does not bring back the descriptions already rewritten with the merchant: it applies to future imports.
intermediaries.add_label: Prefix, as it appears before the asterisk
intermediaries.add_help: For example SUMUP for movements written "SUMUP *BAR ROSSI". Saved descriptions are rewritten right away.
rules.on_intermediary: {n} rules are no longer needed: {rules}. They were written on the payment service (for example PayPal), but the shop you paid now appears instead of the service, so these rules no longer find any movement. You can delete them: if you need a rule, write it on the shop.
check.title: If you want to check
check.intro: One account at a time, from the last movement you checked. I suggest the account furthest behind: you can pick another one and change the date. Come back to the list whenever you like.
check.no_accounts: There are no movements to check yet.
check.all_even: Every account is up to date.
check.transfers_intro: You checked the movements of **{account}**. These transfers did not find their other side: tell me where they went.
check.rule_pending: You are creating a rule: finish it or untick it before saving. The rule also saves the grid's other edits.
check.all_right_confirm: Mark the {n} movements in the grid as checked, as they are?

nav.check.desc: Check your movements one account at a time, from the last one you checked.
nav.expense_confirm.desc: Got a receipt in hand? Tell me date and amount: I find the movement and mark it checked.
expense.title: 🧾 Confirm an expense

expense.placeholder: Date and amount, for example: yesterday, 23.40

expense.ears.progress: Downloading the model that listens to you...
expense.ears.failed: The download did not work: try again whenever you like; meanwhile you can type or dictate.
expense.vt.idle: Press once: then the app manages the turns.

expense.receipts_found: I found {n} movements for receipts you saved. Shall we check them?
